creative.central_question: What do you check before you switch an app to GPT-6.2?
creative.payoff: Test three things we picked from OpenAI's changelog (tool calling, edited conversation history, the instructions field), then read the migration guide.
creative.visual_motif: The signal trace: a cyan request line with a travelling dot leaves the app and routes through an API lane; it returns resolved in the payoff.
creative.music: none (voice only for this dry run)

scenes.narration: Switching to GPT-6.2? Check these three things first.
scenes.motion: headline punches in on 'three'; the cyan signal dot leaves an app box toward a GPT-6.2 box; slow 3% push-in
scenes.visual_description: Headline in the question zone; an app box and a GPT-6.2 box joined by the cyan trace.

scenes.narration: OpenAI released two models, Astra and Sol. Both support the Responses API and Chat Completions.
scenes.motion: two equal neutral variant cards draw on in narration order, then two API lanes connect to both; no ranking or highlight between the cards
scenes.visual_description: Two unbranded, equal-sized cards labelled Astra and Sol, each linked to two lane labels: Responses API and Chat Completions. Source chip: OpenAI changelog, Nov 17 2026.

scenes.narration: The changelog notes differences. We picked three worth testing.
scenes.motion: three empty check boxes appear one by one, labelled 'our pick'; the pinned question stays visible
scenes.visual_description: Pinned question at the top; large 3 with three empty check boxes in amber.

scenes.narration: One. Tool calling requires the Responses API.
scenes.motion: the signal dot travels from the app along a tool-call arrow into the Responses API lane; the Chat Completions lane is shown without a tool-call arrow
scenes.visual_description: S-curve flow: app, then tool-call arrow, then Responses API lane in cyan; a dimmed Chat Completions lane beside it. Source chip: OpenAI changelog.

scenes.narration: Illustrative: if your app calls tools through Chat Completions, tools on GPT-6.2 need the Responses API.
scenes.motion: split view: the illustrative app's tool call is rerouted from the Chat Completions lane to the Responses API lane; neutral colours, no failure styling
scenes.visual_description: Split screen: left lane Chat Completions (muted), right lane Responses API (cyan) with the tool-call arrow; label 'illustrative example'. Source chip: OpenAI changelog.

scenes.narration: Two. In the Responses API, GPT-6.2 changes how reasoning is preserved when you edit earlier messages.
scenes.motion: a stack of message blocks draws on; an earlier block gets an amber edit mark; a 'changed in GPT-6.2' tag appears beside the stack (no mechanism shown)
scenes.visual_description: Vertical stack of four message blocks, amber edit mark on an earlier block, cyan tag 'reasoning preservation changed'. Source chip: OpenAI changelog.

scenes.narration: Three. It also changes how the Responses API handles the top-level instructions field.
scenes.motion: an own-style unbranded request panel appears; the instructions field highlights in cyan and its label pulses once
scenes.visual_description: Generic request panel with fields model, instructions and input; the instructions field highlighted. No vendor UI.

scenes.narration: So test those three before you switch. Then read OpenAI's GPT-6.2 migration guide.
scenes.motion: the three check boxes from scene 3 tick to mint one by one; the signal trace returns resolved and runs on to a migration guide node
scenes.visual_description: Three ticked checks in mint, a trace line from the app ending at a node labelled migration guide. Question pinned and answered.

scenes.narration: The first is a requirement. The other two are behaviour changes worth testing.
scenes.motion: the three checks regroup: check 1 tagged 'requirement', checks 2 and 3 tagged 'behaviour change'; slow push-in
scenes.visual_description: Three check rows with tags: requirement (amber) and behaviour change (cyan) x2. No pass/fail styling.

scenes.narration: Which of these three would your app hit first? Comment below.
scenes.motion: the three numerals 1 2 3 appear and the cyan dot loops from the last numeral back toward the hook's app box so the end can loop to the start
scenes.visual_description: End card with the question and three numbered chips; trace loops to the opening frame.
